reviewer: editorial review against the QC rubric

reasons.hook: Untouched by the rewrite, and still joint best in the batch.
reasons.retention: The slow-down sequence at 0:26 is a genuine investigation beat, which the original did not have - it replaced transit with discovery.
reasons.originality: Recovered. The script is no longer a house-that-keeps-people story; it is an identity story wearing that shape for the first twenty seconds, which is a far less worn position.
reasons.twist: Recovered but not full marks. 'All thirty-one are her' is a real reversal that very few viewers will predict from the opening, though the broader shape - the investigator is the subject - is itself familiar. The locked-door line is what makes it land.
reasons.visual: Unchanged. Doorbell fisheye across ten scenes is still visually monotonous; the overlaid-silhouettes shot helps.

notes: Approved. Visual monotony is the remaining weakness and is a shot-list problem, not a script problem.
rewrite_note: Replaced the predictable payoff. The original ended on 'she has never been recorded leaving either', which the audience reaches by 0:20. The rewrite keeps the hook and the first five lines intact and turns the reversal into identity: every one of the thirty-one arrivals is her. Five captions, five visuals and five prompts rewritten accordingly.
